wine_name: Wind Gap Woodruff Vineyard Pinot Noir, Santa Cruz Mountains
wrong_facts: Hook claims Woodruff Vineyard sits at 1,800 ft — ground truth says it's near Coralitos (which is at ~300-500 ft elevation, not 1,800 ft)
Hook claims 'fractured shale and sandstone' soil — not verified for Woodruff specifically
Hook claims 'Saratoga Gap' funnels wind to this vineyard — Woodruff is near Coralitos in southern Santa Cruz Mountains, far from Saratoga Gap
Claims 2014 crop was 0.9 tons/acre — fabricated number
Claims 15% new François Frères 228-L barrels — fabricated number
Claims pH rarely tops 3.45 — fabricated number
Claims 11 months in oak then six months in stainless — fabricated numbers
Claims diurnal swings of 25°F — fabricated number
Claims berries stay under 23° Brix — fabricated number
Wind Gap started in 2006 — not verified (some sources say different dates)
2013 shows green pepper — unverifiable negative claim about a silver-medal vintage
reasoning: The output is extraordinarily confident and specific, but nearly every number is fabricated — elevation, yield, alcohol, whole-cluster percentage, oak regimen, pH, Brix, prices, aging duration. The hook places Woodruff at 1,800 ft near Saratoga Gap, but ground truth says it's near Coralitos at much lower elevation in the southern Santa Cruz Mountains. This is a provably wrong fact in the hook. The voice is excellent — direct, opinionated, no banned words, great food pairings — but the massive number fabrication triggers the hard penalty cap of 1.5 on correctness. The writing style and specificity are top-tier, which makes the fabrications more dangerous, not less.
